notes:
I couldn't write any notes on Isaiah 14. My first attempt to open the sources (Enduring Word, Precept Austin, the Bible Hub commentary page for v. 12, and Got Questions) was blocked before any page loaded. The tool said I had no web calls left, and my other tools can't reach the internet.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. Since I read nothing, any verse notes I wrote now would come from memory, not the sources, and you'd have no URLs to check them against. So I've left them out.

**What I'll do when web access is back:**

1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word (Isaiah 14), Precept Austin's Isaiah 14 page, and the Bible Hub and StudyLight pages for each verse (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary, Barnes).
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** the main debate is vv. 12–15, the "day star, son of the dawn" (KJV "Lucifer"). Is it about Satan's fall, only about the king of Babylon, or both? I'd look at Calvin's Isaiah commentary on ccel.org, Got Questions, Ligonier or The Gospel Coalition, Wesley's notes on wesley.nnu.edu, a Lutheran source (lcms.org or 1517.org), and Pentecostal teachers (Enduring Word, Sam Storms, ag.org). I'd also look at what they say about vv. 1–2, Israel's return and the nations, which may differ between dispensational and Reformed readers.
3. **Other views:**
   - Bible Odyssey and NET Bible notes on the Hebrew word for "day star" (*Helel*), Canaanite background, Sheol, and the "mount of assembly"
   - New Advent (Church Fathers such as Tertullian and Origen on Lucifer) and Catholic.com
   - OCA for an Orthodox reading
   - Any of these sites discussing the passage in Word of Faith or other popular teaching

Ask again in a new message and I'll run these searches and write the notes in the "v. 4: …" format with a URL for every point.
